my-consortium.title: My consortium place

demoNote: Demo data: every figure is SIMULATED and every commitment or pledge is SAMPLE, not a statement by any named institution.

reasons.pl_no_progress: No progress has been recorded yet

reasons.gr_approved: Approved with an award of {amount} AED (SIMULATED)
reasons.gr_declined: Declined by the HR director (see the note)

reasons.gr_output_submitted: The output is with HR for review
reasons.gr_output_accepted: HR accepted the output as evidence
reasons.gr_output_returned: HR returned the output with a note
reasons.gr_on_behalf: Filed by HR for a placement student with a consent reference
reasons.gr_not_found: No staff record found for you

reasons.gr_early_career: {years} years since hire, under the {max}-year early-career limit
reasons.gr_experienced: {years} years since hire, at or over the {max}-year early-career limit
reasons.gr_placement: A student on an ENEC-sponsored placement (HR files)
reasons.gr_not_staff: Micro-grants are for ENEC staff and placement students
reasons.cc_member_nominated: Nominated; the HR director decides the place
reasons.cc_member_accepted: Place accepted by the HR director
reasons.cc_member_declined: Nomination declined by the HR director
reasons.cc_decline_note: The HR director left a note

reasons.cc_evidence_record: Evidence at level {level} kept on the visit (no Kafa'a skills profile)
reasons.cc_waiting_host: Only the host confirms; evidence follows confirmation

reasons.cc_enec_recent: Hired on {date}, within the last {n} years
reasons.cc_enec_not_recent: Hired on {date}, more than {n} years ago

commit.area: Choose a skill area of the current regional release.
commit.kind: Choose cohort, course change, new course or apprenticeship.
commit.title: Write a title of 5 to 160 characters in English and in Arabic.
commit.summary: Write a summary of 10 to 600 characters in English and in Arabic.
commit.skills: Pick up to eight current catalogue skills (no security skills).
commit.level: Choose a target level from 1 to 4.
commit.plan: Plan one to eight terms from the current term to Feb – Jul 2031, each with 1 to 500 seats.
commit.locked: Terms that have started keep their planned seats.

delivery.term: Choose a term of the plan.
delivery.future: A term that has not started cannot be reported.
delivery.numbers: Enrolled from 0 to 1,000; completed from 0 to the number enrolled.

pledge.people: Enter a whole number of people from 1 to 5,000.
pledge.date: Choose a target date at least 30 days ahead and no later than 31 Dec 2035.
pledge.title: Write a title of 5 to 160 characters in English and in Arabic.
pledge.department: Give the department in English and in Arabic (up to 120 characters), or leave both empty.

progress.date: Choose a date between the pledge date and today.
progress.numbers: Use whole numbers; completed can never be above started.
progress.order: Choose a date later than the last snapshot.
progress.decrease: Started and completed never go down.

rp.intro: ENEC shares its forward skill demand with local universities and training providers as released, suppressed aggregates, and providers answer with planned cohorts and course changes that are tracked against delivery each term.
rp.empty: No regional demand has been released yet
rp.emptyBody: The HR director releases a skill forecast to providers from the release page.
rp.releaseBody: Built from "{name}", shared on {date}. Bands cover the three planning scenarios; the planning scenario is {s}.
rp.noDecision: Planning ranges only: no deployment decision implied, and no individual is ever counted or named.

tile.yearsSub: the plan looks ahead to these years

rp.demandIntro: Working-level holders needed (level 2 or above) and the gap to today's pipeline, in people-equivalents. Cells under {n} are suppressed.
rp.legend: Bar: the gap band across the three scenarios; the mark is the planning-scenario gap. <10 = suppressed.
rp.coverageIntro: Seats your organisation has planned up to Feb – Jul 2031 against each area's planning-scenario gap. Completed counts what you have reported.

how.title: How the released numbers are built
how.body: Only aggregates leave ENEC. Each row sums the released skills of one area from a released skill forecast; skills with fewer than {n} holders are withheld and only counted, and any cell from 1 to 9 is suppressed. Levels, supply, assumptions and people never leave ENEC.

loop.title: The commitment loop
loop.body: Demand signal out, provision commitment back: providers plan cohorts or course changes per academic term, report enrolment and completion each term, and ENEC acknowledges or queries each commitment.

cm.intro: Your organisation's commitments against the regional demand, with the delivery status of each term.
cm.introHr: Every provider's commitments against the regional demand, their delivery status and how far planned seats cover each area's 2030 gap.
cm.emptyProvider: Commit provision against the released demand to start.
cm.emptyBody: Providers have not committed provision yet.

tile.completedSub: a separate count, never added to seats

cm.listIntro: Status is computed from the reported delivery of each term; open Why this? for the terms behind it.
cm.coverage: Coverage of the {y} gap by all providers
cm.coverageIntro: Planned seats up to Feb – Jul 2031 in active commitments against each area's planning-scenario gap in the current release.

how.title: What a commitment records
how.body: A commitment is written only through the commitment service, with an audit entry: planned seats per term, delivery reported per term, ENEC's acknowledgement or query. Terms that have started cannot be re-planned; a withdrawn commitment stays listed with its reason.

cd.intro: Planned seats, reported enrolment and completion per academic term, and the delivery status computed from them.
cd.notFoundBody: It does not exist or belongs to another organisation.
cd.termsIntro: Each started term is compared with its planned seats: 90% or more filled is on track or delivered, 60% or more is at risk or partly delivered, below that is behind or missed.
cd.reportIntro: Report enrolment and completion for a term that has started. A new report for the same term replaces the earlier one.
cd.reportConsequence: ENEC sees the report for {term}; the delivery status is recomputed and the report is audited.
cd.withdrawConsequence: The commitment stays listed as withdrawn with your reason; ENEC's ledger records the change.
cd.reviewIntro: Acknowledge the commitment, or query it with a note the provider will see.
cd.ackConsequence: The provider sees that ENEC acknowledged the commitment.
cd.queryConsequence: The provider sees your note on the commitment.

form.title: Commit provision
form.intro: Answer the released demand with a cohort, a course change, a new course or an apprenticeship, planned per academic term. The check below is the same one the service applies.
form.noSkills: No current catalogue skills in this area.
form.planHint: Leave a term empty to skip it. Terms that have started are locked.
form.consequence: ENEC sees the commitment, its delivery is tracked each term, and the change is audited and written to the ENEC ledger.

rel.intro: Share a released skill forecast with local providers as regional aggregates. Preview exactly what leaves ENEC, compare it with the current release, then release it with a note.
rel.none: No released skill forecast to share
rel.pendingTitle: A newer released forecast is not shared yet
rel.pendingBody: "{name}" was released on {date} and has not been shared with providers.
rel.forecastInfo: Planning scenario {s}; released {date}; {n} skill areas to release.
rel.previewIntro: The rows providers will read, computed with the release rule; the change column compares the planning-scenario gap with the current release.

shared.title: What providers receive
shared.body: Per skill area and year: demand and gap bands across three scenarios, the planning-scenario gap, the skills behind it and how many skills are withheld. Cells from 1 to 9 are suppressed.

never.title: What never leaves ENEC
never.body: Levels, today's supply, assumptions, withheld skill names, security skills and anything about individual people.

rel.notClean: The note may not state headcounts or site information.
rel.isCurrent: This forecast is already the current release.
rel.readOnly: Only the HR director releases regional demand; you can preview it here.
rel.consequence: {n} aggregate rows become visible to every partner and university; the current release is superseded; the release is audited and written to the ENEC ledger.

pl.intro: ENEC departments, suppliers and universities register numeric upskilling pledges: people, skill area and target date. Pledged, started and completed are always shown apart, because a pledge is a commitment, not a completion.
pl.counts: {n} active pledges by {o} organisations, as of {date}.
pl.ledgerIntro: Aggregates only. A cell is suppressed when it holds fewer than {n} people or comes from fewer than {o} organisations.

why.title: Three numbers, never one
why.body: Pledges are promises. Started and completed are counted from dated progress snapshots that only go up. The ledger never adds the three together and never turns a pledge into an achievement.

sup.title: Small counts are suppressed
sup.body: Any cell with 1 to 9 people, or from fewer than {o} organisations, shows <10 instead of a value, so no single organisation's numbers show through. Each organisation sees its own exact numbers on its pledges page.

pr.intro: Your organisation's pledges with exact numbers. Each pledge names your organisation, a skill area and a target date; record progress as dated snapshots.
pr.introHr: Every organisation's pledges with exact numbers (HR view). HR registers and updates pledges for ENEC entities; partners and universities update their own.
pr.hrNote: This view shows every organisation's exact numbers to HR and auditors only. Staff and partners see the suppressed ledger.
pr.recordConsequence: The snapshot is dated, cannot go down later and is audited; the ledger updates.
pr.formOwn: The pledge is registered for your organisation.
pr.formHr: HR registers pledges for ENEC entities.
pr.consequence: The pledge appears in the ledger (suppressed for others) and is audited and written to the ENEC ledger.

gr.scheduleIntro: A new round every two months: the deadline is the 10th of every even month, decisions follow within 14 days and the next round opens the day after the deadline.
gr.simNote: Budgets and awards are SIMULATED demo figures; applicants are synthetic.
gr.purposeHint: What you will learn and how it helps your work (20 to 600 characters, no contact details).
gr.applyConsequence: HR decides after the round deadline, by {date}. You can withdraw until then.
gr.withdrawConsequence: The application stays on record as withdrawn. You can apply again while the round is open.
gr.outputIntro: Within 30 days of the activity ending, share a short report or presentation. When HR accepts it, it becomes validated evidence on the skill you named.
gr.outputSummary: Summary of what you learned and will apply
gr.outputConsequence: HR accepts it as evidence or returns it with a note.
gr.evidenceProfile: Accepted: validated evidence at level {level} added to your skills profile.
gr.evidenceRecord: Accepted: evidence kept on this application (no Kafa'a skills profile).

app.kind: Choose a conference, a short course, a site visit or an exchange.
app.title: Give an activity name of 5 to 160 characters without contact details.
app.purpose: Give a purpose of 20 to 600 characters without contact details.
app.destination: Name the organiser or place (2 to 120 characters, no contact details).
app.dates: The activity starts after the round deadline, within 180 days of it, and lasts up to 30 days.
app.costs: Add one to three cost lines in whole AED, totalling 500 up to the round maximum.
app.skill: Choose a current catalogue skill (not a security skill).
app.output: Promise a report or a presentation.

decision.round_open: Decisions are made after the round deadline.
decision.note: A note of up to 300 characters (at least 5 when declining).
decision.award: An award from 500 up to the amount requested and the round maximum.
decision.budget: This award would take the round over its SIMULATED budget.

output.too_early: Log the output after the activity has ended.
output.kind: Choose a report or a presentation.
output.title: A title of 5 to 160 characters without contact details.
output.summary: A summary of 20 to 1200 characters without contact details.

schedule.exists: The next round is already scheduled.
schedule.budget: A SIMULATED budget from 10,000 to 500,000 AED.
schedule.award: A maximum award from 1,000 to 25,000 AED, not above the budget.
schedule.note: A note of up to 300 characters without contact details.

my.intro: Small, fast grants for early-career staff to attend a conference, a short course, a site visit or an exchange. Rounds run every two months, so there is always a next deadline.
my.already: You have an application in this round. One application per round.
my.noneScheduled: HR has not scheduled the next round yet.
my.eligibleYes: Yes: you can apply in an open round.
my.eligibilityRule: Early-career staff (fewer than 10 years since hire) apply themselves; HR files for students on an ENEC-sponsored placement.
my.mineIntro: Every application with its decision and, once approved, the output you promised.
my.noneBody: Apply in the open round; it takes a few minutes.
my.evidenceBody: An output HR accepts is added as validated evidence on the skill you named (a presentation counts at level 2, a report at level 1).
my.howBody: After the deadline the HR director approves or declines each application within the round's SIMULATED budget, within 14 days. Every decision is audited.

grp.intro: The rolling mobility micro-grant programme in figures. Counts of 1 to 9 are suppressed and no person is named.
grp.rateSub: Of decided applications, with 10 or more decided
grp.acceptedSub: Reports and presentations HR accepted as evidence
grp.roundsIntro: Each round with its window and SIMULATED budget. Cells under {n} are suppressed; money committed shows only behind {n} or more awards.
grp.howBody: A short, predictable cycle lets early-career staff act on an opportunity within weeks instead of waiting for an annual call.
grp.supBody: Any count from 1 to 9 shows as "<{n}" so that no applicant can be singled out.

grh.intro: Decide closed rounds within the SIMULATED budget, review outputs, schedule the next round and file for placement students.
grh.readOnlyBody: You can review every application and decision here; changes are made by HR.
grh.noDecisionsBody: Applications waiting for a decision appear here after their round deadline.
grh.afterDeadline: Decisions open after the deadline on {date}.
grh.approveConsequence: The applicant is notified and the award counts against the round's SIMULATED budget. The decision is audited and recorded in the ledger.
grh.declineConsequence: The applicant sees your note and can apply in a later round. The decision is audited.
grh.ownApplication: Your own application: another HR director decides it.
grh.noOutputsBody: Reports and presentations appear here when grantees submit them.
grh.overdueIntro: Approved grants whose output was due more than 30 days after the activity.
grh.evidenceWill: Accepting adds validated evidence on {skill} at level {level} (ENEC staff only).
grh.acceptConsequence: Validated evidence is written on the named skill and the grantee is notified. Audited and recorded in the ledger.
grh.returnConsequence: The grantee sees your note and can submit again.
grh.ownOutput: You submitted this output: another HR reviewer accepts it.
grh.scheduleConsequence: The round opens on {a} and closes on {b}. Audited and recorded in the ledger.
grh.behalfNoRound: Applications on behalf of placement students are filed in an open round.
grh.behalfTitle: File for a placement student (round to {date})
grh.behalfRule: Students on an ENEC-sponsored placement have no staff account, so HR files for them with their recorded consent. The student's reference and the consent reference are kept on the application.
grh.studentRefHint: The applicant record of a student on an ENEC-sponsored placement.
grh.behalfConfirm: File this application on the student's behalf?
grh.behalfConsequence: Recorded as filed by HR with the consent reference; audited.

cc.intro: Energy employers in the UAE grow one trainee pool together: shared modules hosted in turn at each member's site, a joint project in mixed teams and a mentor from another employer.
cc.simNote: Partner organisations are synthetic; budgets are SIMULATED; partner trainees carry codes, not names.
cc.disclaimer: This cohort design is a demonstration with synthetic partner organisations. It is not an agreement between real employers.
cc.partnersIntro: Each member hosts a module and cross-site visits; a confirmed visit counts as evidence on the site's focus skill.
cc.modulesIntro: Three-day modules, each hosted by a different member.
cc.mentorsIntro: Every trainee is paired with a mentor from a different member organisation. Mentors are shown as role cards.
cc.evidenceRule: Only the host confirms a cross-site visit; the confirmation becomes validated on-the-job evidence for ENEC trainees.
cc.sourcesNote: The cohort pattern follows these programmes; no figure on this page comes from them.

visit.member: The trainee needs an accepted place in this cohort.
visit.host: Choose a host organisation of the cohort.
visit.same_org: A cross-site visit is to another member, not the trainee's own organisation.
visit.date: A date within the cohort, not in the future and in the last 120 days.
visit.module: Choose a module hosted by that organisation, or none.
visit.note: A note of up to 300 characters without contact details.

ccw.intro: Trainees, nominations and cross-site visits for one cohort. Each partner sees only its own trainees; only the host confirms a visit.
ccw.notFoundBody: This cohort does not exist or is not listed.

scope.all: You see every trainee and visit in this cohort.
scope.org: You see only {org}'s trainees and their visits.
scope.own: You see your own place and visits.

ccw.nomClosed: Nominations for this cohort closed on {date}.
ccw.notMemberTitle: Not a member of this cohort
ccw.notMember: Your organisation is not a partner in this cohort, so it cannot nominate trainees.
ccw.nomRuleHr: HR nominates ENEC trainees (active staff at entry level or hired within 5 years) and, on the partner's behalf, trainees of partners without Kafa'a access.
ccw.nomRulePartner: Nominate your own organisation's trainees. They carry a code, not a name; no person record leaves your organisation.
ccw.staffRefHint: The person record of an eligible ENEC staff member.
ccw.nominateConsequence: A trainee code is issued and the HR director decides the place. Audited.
ccw.decideIntro: Accept with a mentor from another member organisation and a project team, or decline with a note.
ccw.ownPlace: Your own nomination: another HR director decides it.
ccw.mentorRule: Only mentors from another member organisation are offered.
ccw.acceptConsequence: The trainee is notified of the mentor and team. Audited and recorded in the ledger.
ccw.declineConsequence: The nominating organisation sees your note. Audited and recorded in the ledger.
ccw.noVisitsBody: Cross-site visits appear here once logged.
ccw.withdrawConsequence: The host will no longer see it to confirm.
ccw.hostRefHint: The host's written confirmation (3 to 80 characters), required when the programme office confirms for a host without Kafa'a access.
ccw.logRule: The trainee, their employer's administrator or the programme office logs a visit to another member's site. The host confirms it.
ccw.noteHint: Up to 300 characters, no contact details.
ccw.logConsequence: The host is asked to confirm it. Evidence is written only after the host confirms.
ccw.hostRule: You see visits to your site with the trainee code and visiting organisation only. Confirm what happened or decline with a reason; you cannot confirm a visit you logged.
ccw.hostEmptyBody: Visits to your site appear here when they are logged.
ccw.hostConfirmConsequence: Writes on-the-job evidence on {skill} (ENEC staff trainees) and notifies the trainee. Audited and recorded in the ledger.
ccw.hostDeclineConsequence: The trainee sees your reason; no evidence is written. Audited.
ccw.figuresNote: Counts under {n} are suppressed so that no trainee can be singled out.

ccm.intro: Your place in the consortium trainee cohort: mentor, project team, the shared modules and your cross-site visits.
ccm.noPlace: You do not hold a consortium place
ccm.noPlaceBody: HR nominates ENEC trainees for each cohort. Talk to your manager if you are interested.
ccm.eligible: You meet the ENEC trainee rule.
ccm.notEligible: ENEC trainees are at entry level or hired within the last {n} years.
ccm.visitsIntro: {n} confirmed by the host. Evidence is written only after the host confirms.
ccm.evidenceWritten: Evidence at level {level} added to your skills profile.
ccm.evidenceRecord: Evidence at level {level} kept on the visit.
ccm.noVisitsBody: Log a visit to another member's site; the host confirms it.
ccm.waiting: The HR director decides your place and names your mentor and team.
